name: Zhang Yiming
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster's Hurun API URL was fetched and returns rank 2 = ByteDance / Social Media / "Zhang Yiming". SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: zh.wikipedia is explicit that he was an EMPLOYEE, not a founder, at Kuxun (joined Feb 2006 as one of the first engineers, technical director 2007), Microsoft (2008) and Fanfou (2008-09, technical partner); his FIRST independent venture was 99fang (九九房), a vertical real-estate search company founded Oct 2009 ("这是其首次独立创业项目"), which he left as CEO in 2011-12 to start ByteDance. No earlier crossing found for 99fang: it never published revenue, was a small venture-backed mobile property-search app, and no source describes it at meaningful commercial scale; the 2011 bar was $6,986,920 (RMB ~45.2m at 6.4630), which a vertical property app of that size did not plausibly reach. Recorded here rather than assumed: two searches found no revenue figure for 99fang at all. REV10: jiemian.com (界面新闻) states "今日头条在 2014 年的广告营收是 3 亿人民币" -- RMB 300m advertising revenue in 2014, the first year Toutiao was commercialised (2015: RMB 1.5bn; 2016: >=RMB 6bn per the same article). CURRENCY CONVERSION: 2014 annual average USD/CNY 6.1428 -> RMB 300m = US$48.8m, against the 2014 constant-2026 rev10 bar of $7,353,351. Margin is enormous (6.6x), so the only real question is whether the crossing was 2013 rather than 2014; ByteDance was founded Mar 2012, Toutiao launched Aug 2012 and monetisation began in 2014, so 2013 revenue was far below the 2013 bar ($7,235,970 = RMB ~44.8m at 6.1958). Exact 2014 recorded rather than a 2012-2014 bound because the source names 2014 as the first commercialisation year. IPO/acq fallback not used and not needed. a6: zh.wikipedia -- by 2018 ByteDance was valued at US$75bn, passing Uber as the world's most valuable startup.

name: Bo Lu
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: ycombinator.com/companies/futureadvisor names FutureAdvisor, batch Summer 2010, founder Bo Lu, San Francisco, "Acquired by BlackRock (NYSE:BLK) post Series B in 2015". SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: no earlier venture found. Sourced sequence is UIUC computer science (highest honours) -> Microsoft product planner/program manager 2004-2010 -> FutureAdvisor, co-founded with Jon Xu in the YC S10 batch. His other operating role, COO of Clipboard Health, came AFTER FutureAdvisor. FALLBACK acq50 USED, AND IT IS THE RARE PERMITTED CASE. frame.md bars the fallback only where an earlier rev10 crossing is known; here the sources positively establish the opposite. RIABiz reports FutureAdvisor at roughly $650m AUM on a 50-basis-point fee, giving "about $3 million in revenue", with ~50 employees and $21m of venture funding raised; Bo Lu's own 2015 interview says the company expected to reach profitability only at $1B in AUM. Against the 2015 constant-2026 rev10 bar of $7,362,080, ~$3m is well under half, and even $1B AUM at 50bp would be ~$5m -- still below the bar. So no rev10 crossing ever occurred and there is nothing earlier to date. ACQ50: BlackRock announced the acquisition 26 Aug 2015; RIABiz puts the price at $152 million, kitces.com at $150m+, against the 2015 constant-2026 acq50 bar of $36,810,398 -- 4.1x the bar, not close. a1: two source attempts (interviews, YC and advisory-firm bios) produced no birth year; he states only that he came to the US from China at age seven. a6: no later scale marker distinct from the acquisition; he ran FutureAdvisor as a BlackRock Solutions unit for four more years.

name: Ma Huateng
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster's Hurun API URL was fetched and returns rank 3 = Tencent / Gaming, Telecoms / "Ma Huateng". SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK: no earlier venture found. en.wikipedia gives an unbroken employee track from the 1993 Shenzhen University BSc -- China Motion Telecom Development (pager-system software, US$176/month) then Shenzhen Runxun Communications -- to the Nov 1998 co-founding of Tencent with four classmates. Two searches surfaced no company founded by him before Tencent; his pre-Tencent side income was personal stock trading and stock-market software, not a venture entity. REV10: jiemian.com (界面新闻, 腾讯游戏帝国之发轫2003) states Tencent's 2001 annual revenue was "近5000万" (approaching RMB 50m) with net profit "超过1000万" (over RMB 10m), 2001 being the year Tencent turned profitable off the China Mobile 移动梦网 SP business. CURRENCY CONVERSION: 2001 annual average USD/CNY 8.2771 -> RMB 49m = US$5.92m, against the 2001 constant-2026 rev10 bar of $5,500,974. MARGIN UNDER 20% -- about +8% (the range implied by "近5000万", RMB 48-50m, is US$5.80-6.04m, above the bar throughout, but thinly). 2000 is sourced below the bar qualitatively and decisively: Chinese accounts of 2000 describe Tencent with RMB 10,000 left in the bank at its worst and QQ with no commercial revenue source at all before the SP era, against a 2000 bar of $5,348,773 = RMB ~44.3m at 8.2784. Exact 2001 recorded rather than a 2000-2001 bound. IPO/acq fallback barred and not used. a6: Tencent's June 2004 Hong Kong listing.

name: Huang Zheng
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster's Hurun API URL was fetched and returns rank 7 = Pinduoduo / E-Commerce / "Huang Zheng". SERIAL FOUNDER CALL -- THE HIT IS NOT PINDUODUO. Huang founded four ventures in sequence: Ouku.com (欧酷网, consumer-electronics B2C, founded 2007 on leaving Google, sold to LightInTheBox/兰亭集势 for US$2.2m in 2010); Leqi (乐其, e-commerce agency/TP, 2009-10, later the largest maternal-infant TP on Tmall); Shanghai Xunmeng (上海寻梦信息技术, games, founded 2013, "每年贡献上千万元利润"); and Pinhaohuo/Pinduoduo (April 2015). The FIRST to cross is Ouku, so the roster's famous entity is not the hit entity. REV10: niaogebiji.com, republishing the Tencent News piece 从滨江这家企业开始，黄峥就没输过, states "三年后，欧酷成为手机和电子教育品类排名前三的电商网站，年营收超过了6000万" -- three years after the 2007 founding, Ouku's ANNUAL REVENUE (年营收, not GMV) exceeded RMB 60m. CURRENCY CONVERSION: RMB 60m at the 2010 annual average USD/CNY 6.7695 = US$8.86m against the 2010 constant-2026 rev10 bar of $6,773,124 (+31%); read as 2009 instead, at 6.8310 it is US$8.78m against the 2009 bar of $6,663,819 (+32%). Above the bar on either reading. BOUNDED 2007-2010, span 3 years: lower end is Ouku's sourced 2007 founding (a company cannot earn before it exists, per frame.md), upper end is the RMB 60m figure, dated "three years after" the founding and capped by the 2010 sale. The exact crossing year inside that window is not published. IPO/acq fallback barred: an earlier crossing is known. a6: Pinduoduo's July 2018 Nasdaq listing.

name: Fred Smith
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster's Forbes billionaires API URL returned a service error when fetched, but forbes.com/profile/frederick-smith names him under "2025 Billionaires" -- "Founder and Executive Chairman, FedEx", net worth $5.8B as of 4/1/25, source "FedEx, Self Made", self-made score 7. SERIAL FOUNDER CHECK -- Arkansas Aviation Sales considered and rejected as the hit entity. In 1969-70 Smith bought a CONTROLLING INTEREST in Ark Aviation Sales, an existing aircraft-maintenance business at Little Rock's Adams Field owned by his stepfather/father-in-law, and by 1971 had turned it into a used corporate-jet dealer posting "over $9 million in revenue and the company's seeing profits for the first time" (encyclopedia.com). That is far above the 1971 bar of $1,257,987 -- but it is a going concern he bought into rather than a venture he started, which frame.md and this dataset's existing rows treat as unable to fire rev10 however large it was; and its pre-Smith revenue is undocumented, so even on the other reading no crossing year could be sourced or bounded and the row would be crossing_undatable rather than dated to AAS. Federal Express, incorporated 18 June 1971, is his first FOUNDED venture. REV10 BOUNDED 1973-1975, span 2. Lower end: FedEx's first-production year -- service began 17 April 1973 to 25 cities with 14 Dassault Falcons and 389 employees, and it cannot have earned before it flew (frame.md allows the founding/first-production year as a lower bound). Upper end: fundinguniverse's FedEx corporate history, "in 1975 alone it gained $43.5 million in sales against an $11.5 million loss", against the 1975 constant-2026 rev10 bar of $1,671,103 -- 26x the bar, so the margin is not close. The exact crossing year inside the window is not published: FedEx's fiscal year ended 31 May, so FY1973 held only six weeks of operations, and two searches found no FY1974 revenue figure. All figures USD, no conversion needed. IPO fallback not used (an earlier crossing is known); a6 is the 1978 NYSE listing. Note this row is dated on rev10, not rank1 -- revenue exists for this firm, so the bucket's volume-ranking fallback does not apply.
